summary: Both are the same pattern — the whole strip, spatially uniform, breathing pure red from black to full and back — but the port's breath is a linear triangle wave with a 29.5 s period where the original's is a smooth sinusoid with a 32.8 s period.
observations: Structure: identical on both sides. Every pixel of the 60-px strip holds the same value in every frame I dumped (t=0,4,8,12,16,20,24,29.4,44 s: orig min==max and port min==max at all nine times), so there is no spatial structure at all — just a global brightness envelope. Confirmed again on an 8x8 grid override (label grid8-recheck): both sides render a flat, uniform square.

Color: identical. Pure red on both — meanG and meanB are exactly 0 for every frame of every run, on both sides, and the per-pixel dumps show G=B=0. Both sweep the full range, orig 0..254 and port 0..252/254 peak.

Rhythm — period: original ~32.8 s per breath, port ~29.5 s, i.e. the port runs ~11% fast. Measured over 240 s (label survey-240, 8 peaks / 7 troughs each side): orig maxima at 7.5, 40.5, 73.0, 106.0, 139.0, 171.5, 204.5, 237.0 s -> 32.79 s spacing; port maxima at 14.3, 43.8, 73.3, 102.8, 132.3, 161.8, 191.3, 220.8 s -> 29.50 s spacing. Troughs give the same two numbers. Neither side drifts; both are perfectly periodic out to 240 s.

Rhythm — waveform shape: the original's fade is sinusoidal, the port's is a linear triangle. Sampling meanR once a second (fps10-60s), the port's rise is a constant ~17.4 counts/s (1, 19, 36, 53, 70, 88, 105, 122, 140, 157, 174, 191, 209, 226, 243) and it turns around sharply at both ends; the original's rise decelerates into the peak and out of the trough (129, 154, 177, 198, 217, 233, 244, 252, 254, 253, 246 ...  and 14, 5, 0, 0, 5, 14, 28 through the trough). Quarter-cycle check between orig's peak (t=8.15) and trough (t=24.52): at t=12.2 orig reads 220 where a linear ramp would give 190 and a raised cosine 217; at t=20.4 orig reads ~38 where linear would give 63 and cosine 37. The port matches the linear prediction at the equivalent points. Visually this shows in the rhythm waterfall as wider, softer black and full-red bands on the original versus a thinner, sharper black band and a narrower bright line on the port.

Phase: with the harness's pinned clock the original starts mid-rise (meanR 129 at t=0) and the port starts from its minimum (meanR 1 at t=0, trough centred at t=0.05). The original's minima land at 24.0/57.0/89.5... s, the port's at 29.0/58.5/88.0... s. On real hardware the absolute phase of a breathe is not really observable, so I weight this far below the period and shape findings, but it does suggest the port's phase is anchored to run start while the original's follows absolute time.

Both sides are frame-rate independent (time-based, not frame-stepped): rendering each side at 5, 10 and 20 fps puts its peaks and troughs at the same absolute times (orig peak ~8.1 s and trough ~24.5 s at all three rates; port peak ~14.7 s and trough ~29.4 s at all three). No frame-rate-coupling bug on either side.
Both sides are fully deterministic and seed-independent: seed 7 versus seed 1 gives a total meanR difference of exactly 0 over 300 frames on both sides. Nothing stochastic here.
No modes or regimes: over 240 s at 2 fps both sides show one repeating breath and nothing else — no second look, no palette walk, no amplitude drift.
Control surface matches: the engine reports zero settable controls on BOTH sides (probe run: 'no settable controls' for orig and port). No missing or extra dial.

Alive on both sides: no compile errors, no runtime errors in any run. The high zeroMotionFrames counts in the 6 s baseline (orig 111/120, port 120/120) are just the fade being slower than one 8-bit count per frame at 20 fps, not a freeze — the 60 s runs show both sides moving continuously.
feedback: Slow the port's breath by ~11%: the port completes a full black-to-full-to-black cycle in 29.5 s, the original takes 32.8 s. Measured from 8 consecutive peaks over a 240 s window, so it is not a windowing artefact.

Change the port's brightness envelope from a linear triangle to a sinusoid (raised cosine). The port ramps at a constant ~17.4 counts/s and reverses instantly at both ends; the original eases in and out, dwelling visibly near full red and near black. Concretely, one quarter-cycle after its peak the original still reads ~217/254 where the port reads ~190/254, and one quarter-cycle before its trough the original reads ~37 where the port reads ~63. This is the only difference a viewer would actually notice: the original 'hangs' at the extremes, the port slides through them.

Everything else is already exact and should not be touched: spatially uniform output (identical value on every pixel), pure red with green and blue at exactly 0, full 0..255 amplitude, time-based (fps-invariant) animation, no controls, and no randomness.
